title: Linear algebra, conditioning and nonunique solutions
outcome: Solve small linear systems, inspect residuals and distinguish a fitted prediction from an identified coefficient vector.

exercises.title: Verify a solution
exercises.task: Multiply the computed vector by the original matrix.
exercises.hint: Keep the original equation and units visible.
exercises.answer: A residual is a useful numerical check but must be interpreted alongside conditioning.

exercises.title: Reuse a factorization
exercises.task: Double the right-hand side without refactorizing.
exercises.expected: The solution doubles for this linear system.
exercises.answer: Reusable factorization separates setup from repeated solves.

exercises.title: Expose nonidentification
exercises.expected: Predictions on the design remain unchanged.
exercises.hint: The displacement lies in the null space.
exercises.answer: Fitted-value agreement does not uniquely identify every parameter.

exercises.title: Interpret a pseudoinverse
exercises.task: Compare coefficient norms in case B.
exercises.expected: The pseudoinverse solution has smaller norm than the shifted alternative.
exercises.hint: Minimum norm is a selection rule among compatible solutions.
exercises.answer: It does not supply missing scientific identification assumptions.

exercises.title: Use the correct transpose
exercises.task: Compare adjoint and transpose for the complex vector.
exercises.answer: Matching dimensions alone is insufficient to choose the correct complex inner-product convention.

exercises.title: Assess sensitivity
exercises.task: Perturb an ill-conditioned problem before trusting its coefficients.
exercises.expected: Inspect conditioning as well as residuals.
exercises.hint: A small residual need not imply stable parameters.
exercises.answer: Numerical accuracy and scientific interpretation require the appropriate assumptions and scales.
